column1: # confinement-coverage.tsv (harbor#1300, #555 P3) — for every admission rule in standards/naming/controls.tsv,
# whether the confinement already denies its target. `covered`: a confined Bash call skips the rule once the operator's
# install turns the skip on (harbor.toml `confinement_skip = "true"`, then sudo sh bin/deploy-confinement.sh); the
# guard records `covered` and the sandbox decides. `judged`: the rule always runs. No rule is deleted here: un-covering
# WHY A SIBLING FILE AND NOT A controls.tsv COLUMN (the ticket asked for a column). A column changes the controls.tsv
# header, which every pack's controls fragment must equal byte for byte (bin/pack.sh), so the private layer's pack would
# refuse to install until it moved in lockstep. This file names every admission id instead, and the suite fails when
# the two id sets differ, or when the covered rows differ from floor_confinement_covers in bin/library-admission.sh.
# NEVER COVERED: a rule whose target can sit in the write zone ($PORT_ROOT, deliverables_dir, the temp trees) or above
# the config dir, a remote action, a file tool (the sandbox wraps Bash alone), or anything that is not a file write.
